old_texts.text: My family had been prominent, well-to-do people in this Middle Western city for three generations. I graduated from New Haven in 1915, then took part in that delayed Teutonic migration called the Great War — and I enjoyed the counter-raid so thoroughly that I came back restless.

old_texts.text: The Middle West now seemed the ragged edge of the universe — so I decided to go East and learn the bond business. Father agreed to finance me for a year, and in the spring of twenty-two I came East, permanently, I thought. The practical thing was rooms in the city; but when a young man at the office suggested we take a house together in a commuting town, it sounded like a great idea.
